title: 2002 AMC 10A Problem 19
statement: Spot’s doghouse has a regular hexagonal base that measures one yard on each side. He is tethered to a vertex with a two-yard rope. What is the area, in square yards, of the region outside the doghouse that Spot can reach?

solutions.text:
At the tether vertex the hexagon blocks its \(120^\circ\) interior angle, leaving a \(240^\circ\) sector of radius \(2:\) area \(\dfrac{240}{360}\pi(2)^2=\dfrac{8\pi}{3}.\)

Wrapping around each of the two adjacent vertices, \(1\) yard of rope remains and sweeps a \(60^\circ\) sector: \(2\cdot\dfrac{60}{360}\pi(1)^2=\dfrac{\pi}{3}.\) The total is \(\dfrac{8\pi}{3}+\dfrac{\pi}{3}=3\pi.\)

Thus, the correct answer is E.
hints: The interior angle of a regular hexagon is \(120^\circ,\) so Spot sweeps \(240^\circ\) at radius \(2\)
Around each adjacent vertex the leftover \(1\) yard of rope sweeps a \(60^\circ\) sector
